Initiator amino acyl-tRNA fᴹᵉᵗ only enters through the A-site of a ribosome
Permitted wobble base-pairing (tRNA anticodon first position ↔ mRNA codon third position): G pairs with U or C; U pairs with A or G; Inosine (I) pairs with U, C, or A.

qs.q: What was the primary function discovered for tRNA when it was isolated and identified by Robert W. Holley in 1959?
o: Defending bacterial cells against invading bacteriophages
Playing a critical role in protein synthesis via amino acids
Serving as the primary catalytic site for protein synthesis
Carrying genetic information from the nucleus to cytoplasm
qs.e: Robert W. Holley isolated and identified transfer RNA (tRNA), which plays a critical role in protein synthesis. Ribosomes, discovered by George Palade, serve as the actual site of protein synthesis.

qs.q: During an analysis of protein synthesis elongation in a eukaryotic cell culture, an investigator tracks the precise locations of various tRNAs on the ribosome. Which ribosomal locus holds the tRNA with the growing polypeptide chain?
o: Aminoacyl-tRNA binding site
Acceptor stem binding site
Peptidyl transferase locus
Peptidyl-tRNA holding site
qs.e: The P (peptidyl) site holds the tRNA with the growing polypeptide chain. The A site binds incoming aminoacyl-tRNA, and the E site is where empty tRNA exits.

qs.q: Which enzyme is responsible for catalyzing the attachment of a specific amino acid to its corresponding tRNA molecule?
o: RNA polymerase II enzyme activity
Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase enzyme activity
Release factor protein activity
Peptidyl transferase enzyme activity
qs.e: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase catalyzes the attachment of amino acids to their specific tRNA molecules. There are different synthetases for each of the 20 standard amino acids.

qs.q: What is the term used to describe a tRNA molecule that has been mistakenly attached to the wrong amino acid?
o: Charged tRNA with a correct amino acid
Acylated tRNA bound to a carrier molecule
Uncharged tRNA lacking any amino acid
Mischarged tRNA with an incorrect amino acid
qs.e: A mischarged tRNA is one that is mistakenly attached to the wrong amino acid, which requires hydrolytic editing proofreading mechanisms to correct. Charged or acylated tRNA refers to correctly loaded molecules.

qs.q: A geneticist is evaluating how biological systems efficiently translate 61 different sense codons using a smaller repertoire of approximately 45 distinct tRNA molecules. What fundamental mechanism explains this observation?
o: Exclusive binding to the Shine-Dalgarno sequence
Flexible base pairing at the third codon position
Continuous hydrolytic editing of incorrect amino acids
Premature translation termination by release factors
qs.e: The wobble hypothesis explains that the third base of the codon can pair with more than one nucleotide, enabling fewer tRNA molecules to recognize multiple codons. Modified nucleotides like inosine further enhance this flexibility.

qs.q: What specific amino acid is carried by the special initiator tRNA during translation initiation in prokaryotes?
o: Methionine carried by initiator tRNA
N-formylmethionine carried by initiator tRNA
Leucine carried by initiator tRNA
Glycine carried by initiator tRNA
qs.e: In prokaryotes, the initiator tRNA carries N-formylmethionine (fMet), whereas in eukaryotes, the initiator tRNA carries standard methionine (Met). Both bind to the start codon AUG.

qs.q: A researcher is studying the wobble hypothesis to understand how fewer than 61 tRNA molecules can translate all sense codons. In this mechanism, what is the primary structural characteristic of the wobble position?
o: The last base of the anticodon is modified by synthetase
The third base of the codon pairs flexibly with nucleotides
The first base of the anticodon forms covalent bonds
The middle base of the codon undergoes hydrolytic editing
qs.e: The wobble position is the third base of the codon, which can pair with more than one nucleotide to allow fewer tRNA molecules to recognize multiple codons. Covalent bonding does not occur at this position during codon-anticodon pairing.

qs.q: During an experiment investigating translation fidelity, a scientist notes that a specific tRNA anticodon contains the modified base inosine. Which set of bases can inosine pair with on mRNA codons according to the study notes?
o: Uracil, adenine, or cytosine bases
Adenine, thymine, or uracil bases
Cytosine, thymine, or guanine bases
Guanine, cytosine, or adenine bases
qs.e: Inosine is a modified base found in some tRNA anticodons that can pair with uracil, adenine, or cytosine on mRNA codons to increase pairing flexibility. Thymine is a DNA base and is not found in mRNA codons.
